Job Title:
Chief Advancement Officer

Job Type: Full Time

Location: San Francisco

Salary: $325,000 – $350,000

Job Summary

The California Academy of Sciences seeks a Chief Advancement Officer to lead a division at an inflection point. The Academy is a scientifically rigorous, globally respected institution moving through a period of real change, including two rounds of layoffs, a newly ratified collective bargaining agreement, and a period of heightened external scrutiny. Despite these challenges, the internal culture and momentum are improving and reflect enthusiasm for the future. This is a hands-on role for a builder who can stabilize and re-energize a large, talented division and forge real partnerships with scientists, educators, and Board members who are eager to be activated as partners in philanthropy.

Looking ahead, the Academy is building towards a comprehensive campaign spanning capital, operating, and endowment priorities. The incoming Chief of Advancement will help shape this campaign’s scope and sequencing from the ground up, in close partnership with the Executive Director and Board.

The Academy is concurrently conducting a search for its next Executive Director. The Chief of Advancement hire is expected to serve as a compatible, strong, activating fundraising partner to the incoming Executive Director, especially in the early days of that transition.

Full Job Description

THIS POSITION IS HYBRID. THE SUCCESSFUL CANDIDATE WILL BE IN THE SAN FRANCISCO OFFICE FOUR DAYS A WEEK.

About The California Academy Of Sciences

Founded in 1853, the California Academy of Sciences (the Academy) is a globally renowned, AZA-accredited non-profit scientific and cultural institution located in the heart of San Francisco’s Golden Gate Park. Home to a world-class planetarium, aquarium, rainforest, research institute, and natural history museum—all under one living roof—the Academy’s mission is to regenerate the natural world through science, learning, and collaboration.

The Academy’s living collection reflects Earth’s vast biodiversity, consisting of nearly 60,000 animals representing over 800 species. Its research collections are the largest west of the Mississippi, spanning nearly 46 million plants, animals, fossils, and cultural artifacts from across the globe and throughout history. Its diverse team includes leading biodiversity scientists, educators, storytellers, designers, and communicators who are passionate about advancing knowledge and catalyzing action through science and storytelling.

Organizational Culture

The California Academy of Sciences invites new staff members to join as part of a mission-driven community that values curiosity, collaboration, and innovation, and celebrates its accomplishments together. Staff share a commitment to executing a new strategic plan that will strengthen the organization’s financial foundations, cultivate a vibrant internal culture, and foster smart growth to secure the Academy’s future.

The Academy is looking for candidates who excel in their field and take pride in their work. Candidates may come from a number of different backgrounds and experiences and are encouraged to apply whether or not you believe you meet every competency for the position.

OPPORTUNITY HIGHLIGHTS

Salary Range: $325,000 – $350,000

Benefits Include

5 weeks of vacation, in addition to holidays, sick time, and floating holidays

Medical, Vision, Dental Insurance

403b

YOU ARE

An enthusiastic, activating doer with strong personal follow-through

An enterprise thinker who partners naturally across science, education, communications, and governance

A leader who embodies a growth mindset, with proven experience demonstrating success

A talented, respected, and gifted storyteller

A thoughtful and generous leader who supports and promotes their team

Deeply rooted in Bay Area philanthropy

Position Overview

The California Academy of Sciences seeks a Chief Advancement Officer to lead a division at an inflection point. The Academy is a scientifically rigorous, globally respected institution moving through a period of real change, including two rounds of layoffs, a newly ratified collective bargaining agreement, and a period of heightened external scrutiny. Despite these challenges, the internal culture and momentum are improving and reflect enthusiasm for the future. This is a hands-on role for a builder who can stabilize and re-energize a large, talented division and forge real partnerships with scientists, educators, and Board members who are eager to be activated as partners in philanthropy.

Looking ahead, the Academy is building towards a comprehensive campaign spanning capital, operating, and endowment priorities. The incoming Chief of Advancement will help shape this campaign’s scope and sequencing from the ground up, in close partnership with the Executive Director and Board.

The Academy is concurrently conducting a search for its next Executive Director. The Chief of Advancement hire is expected to serve as a compatible, strong, activating fundraising partner to the incoming Executive Director, especially in the early days of that transition.

REPORTING RELATIONSHIP

The Chief Advancement Officer reports to the Executive Director and serves as a member of the Senior Leadership Team. The role oversees a division of approximately 18-20 staff organized across leadership giving, corporate & foundation partnerships, donor events, planned giving, and development operations.

Primary Responsibilities

Fundraising Strategy & Revenue Growth

Build and lead a culture of philanthropy across the Advancement division and the institution as a whole

Ensure direct, trusted working relationships with scientists, educators, and Board members and activate them as partners in fundraising

Identify fundraising needs across existing programs and build attainable near- and long-term strategies spanning annual giving, capital campaigns, planned giving, special events, and endowment

Explore new revenue streams by evaluating and refining donor solicitation, cultivation, communication, and recognition/affinity programs, as a way to keep donors informed and connected to the Academy’s mission, work, and accomplishments

Regularly evaluate and adjust fundraising strategies, leveraging internal relationships and Board members to increase revenue and participation, and recommend cultivation and solicitation visits to major donors and prospects

Take a hands-on, active role with major and strategic donors and maintain ongoing communication with executive leadership and the Board to ensure buy-in to fundraising initiatives at the highest level

Portfolio Management & Board Relations

Work closely with the Board of Directors and Advancement Committee chair and members to identify, cultivate, and shepherd board member solicitations

Support Board members in every aspect of their philanthropic journey, including their personal commitment to the Academy and their relationships with various public and private funders and philanthropists

Staff and prepare the Board in a strategy for increased participation and eventual campaigns

Lead a traditional advancement portfolio, including annual fund, membership, major and principal gifts, and planned giving

Maintain a personal portfolio of the organization’s most sophisticated and generous donors

Position the division for a comprehensive campaign

Diversification of Funding Sources

Evaluate and grow corporate and foundation partnerships alongside individual giving, including sponsorship and IP-partnership opportunities

Support pursuit of government, agency, and institutional grant funding in partnership with science and program leadership

Expand planned giving and endowment strategies to diversify the Academy’s long-term funding base

Development Operations, Technology, & Data

Oversee development operations, including the donor database/CRM, gift processing, and prospect research infrastructure

Use data and reporting to inform fundraising strategy, track progress against goals, and support Board- and Senior Leadership Team-level decision-making

Evaluate current systems and processes for opportunities to improve efficiency and staff productivity

Team Leadership & Internal Management

Recruit, coach, nurture, and retain a high-performing team; provide an environment that encourages stability as well as a growth mindset, while holding the team accountable to ambitious goals

Provide leadership that challenges, inspires, and motivates people across the Academy’s local, national, and global community

Demonstrate a proven ability to recruit, mentor, lead, and develop a diverse staff, with a track record of building high-performing, loyal teams

Lead with a flexible, inclusive style that adapts to different audiences and sharpens colleagues’ focus

Serve as a positive, unifying figure who leads by influence and example to build an integrated development culture across the Academy

Demonstrate a commitment to transparency that builds trust and confidence in the advancement operation across the institution

Manage the division’s budget, staffing, and day-to-day operations

Serve as a steady, credible, and enthusiastic voice on the Senior Leadership Team during a period of institutional change

Foster a culture of respect, communication, and accountability within the team

Champion the Academy’s culture of equity, diversity, and inclusion, bringing commitment, ideas, and energy to diversity efforts across the workforce, donor base, and broader community

COMPETENCIES

Mission alignment and a genuine commitment to youth, science, learning, and curiosity

15+ years of progressively challenging fundraising experience, including 5 or more years of senior management

Comprehensive campaign experience

Bachelor’s degree required; advanced degrees, certifications, and/or other advanced education, highly regarded

Background in museums, conservation, science, or education-adjacent fundraising, preferred

Proven success soliciting and maintaining a portfolio of six- and seven-figure gifts

Experience working within the San Francisco Bay Area philanthropic community

Ideal Candidate Statement

The ideal candidate is a seasoned information technology executive with at least five years of progressively responsible experience leading an information technology department, and a current Certified Information Systems Security Professional (CISSP) or Certified Information Security Manager (CISM) demonstrating deep expertise in cybersecurity, infrastructure, and regulatory compliance. They combine strategic, big-picture thinking with hands-on operational skill, equally comfortable setting districtwide technology vision, managing budgets and vendor contracts, and directing the day-to-day security, network, and systems work that keeps a college running. This person mentors and develops technical staff, builds trust across administrators, staff, faculty and governance committees, and communicates complex technical issues clearly to non-technical stakeholders. Above all, they bring a genuine, equity-minded commitment to serving a culturally diverse community college population, along with the adaptability and independent judgment needed to navigate evolving technology, risk, and public policy landscapes.

Position Description

Under the direction of the Vice President, Administrative Services, the Executive Director of Information Technology Services provides districtwide leadership and technology planning. The incumbent manages a highly skilled workforce including technical and management level staff in a culturally diverse environment and works collaboratively to support faculty innovation in academic learning environments. The Executive Director of Information Technology Services plans, organizes, controls, and directs the technology operations for the college. The incumbent provides technical recommendations regarding hardware and software for the district for both instructional and administrative use. In addition, the incumbent provides executive oversight for the college's information security program, leads the strategic design, implementation and enforcement of policies to protect critical data, mitigate cyber risk and ensure compliance with regulatory standards.

Technology Operations Management: Provides strategic technical guidance to the Vice President of Administrative Services, assessing institutional IT needs and recommending solutions. Oversees and improves information services, including distance education support, telecommunications, networking, classroom technology, and user support. Administers a district-wide IT infrastructure and integrated systems (e.g., Colleague and third-party products), ensuring service alignment with instructional and administrative needs. Implements and manages infrastructure and application projects using project management best practices. Oversees key systems such as website, email, backups, virtual environments, and networks (wired, wireless, and telecommunications). Ensures accessibility compliance across all district-wide IT systems.
Oversight of Information Security: Evaluates the college's information security needs and implements information security measures to protect the information and technology resources of the district; Works with third party vendors as needed and with district departments to mitigate risks and threats to information security. Develops procedures for an annual information security audit and leads the review in coordination with other essential departments. Advises executive leadership of results and risks. Coordinates with Risk Management and Campus Police Services and other law enforcement agencies to report and resolve information security incidents.
Information Technology Staff Management: Provide guidance, leadership, and mentoring to a team of professionals. Plan for and manage recruitment, orientation, and continued training and education of staff to support and develop the technical expertise needed to meet long-term business needs. Manage staff by reviewing, approving and allocating work and work assignments. Prepares cost estimates and specifications for purchase and maintenance of college technology assets and develop RFQs and RFPs for information system and technology related services. Evaluate materials, products and services. Recommend and implement technology related acquisitions. Engages in the district's program review process to assess workload and staffing, administrative support systems, internal reporting relationships, and technology needs. Identifies and implements approved program improvement objectives to further enhance the efficiency and effectiveness of service delivery methods and procedures.

The Downtown Modesto Partnership (DMP) is recruiting for its Executive Director to lead the organization. We are seeking a passionate, dedicated leader to steward our mission to create a vibrant community through activities and partnerships designed to improve the quantity of quality experiences in downtown Modesto.

Overview of the Position

The Executive Director reports directly to the Board of Directors and is supported by a team of staff and contract technical experts. The Executive Director must provide oversight and direction to ensure the successful execution of the team in support of the overall organizational goals.

The Executive Director is responsible for the following:

Representing DMP - Serve as the lead public spokesperson for the organization, engaging downtown Modesto property owners to ensure the organization is meeting their needs, developing strategic relationships across all relevant public and private sectors, and exercise all responsibilities in a professional manner.

Leading DMP Strategies - Provide strategic direction to ensure the successful day-to-day management, growth, and sustainability of DMP. 

Leading DMP Team – Develop the DMP team to ensure business strategies, programs, policies, resources, and overall direction for the organization are being developed in alignment with DMP’s mission, utilizing every available resource. 

Protecting DMP Assets – Maintain oversight of DMP risk management and compliance with all statutory, regulatory, and ethical requirements regarding bylaws, policies, finance, employee health, safety, and employment.

Specific Job Responsibilities

Serve as the public face of Downtown Modesto, building partnerships with government agencies, businesses, nonprofits, and community organizations while fostering meaningful community engagement and advocacy.

Provide overall organizational leadership, serving as the primary driver of organizational success, strategic planning, Board engagement, and accountability for achieving mission-aligned results.

Direct implementation of DMP programs, ensuring effective delivery of cleaning, maintenance, beautification, marketing, and safety initiatives while using performance metrics and data to continuously improve outcomes.

Oversee the stewardship and management of DMP finances, including ensuring compliance with federal, state, and local regulations and Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (GAAP) applicable to a 501c3 nonprofit organization.

Maintain an inclusive working relationship with the Board of Directors, staff, members, partners, and vested stakeholders that emphasizes open dialogue, complete transparency, professional rapport, and a unified approach. 

Supervise DMP staff, including providing guidance and oversight into their day-to-day responsibilities, mentoring each person to grow in their roles for their benefit as well as that of the business, conducting their annual performance evaluation, and providing constructive discipline, if necessary, in compliance with the DMP Employee Handbook.

Oversee the development, implementation, and management of effective human resources, safety, and risk management programs, including compliance with all federal, state, and local regulations, as well as fostering a positive, productive, and proactive work environment.

Assist the Board of Directors in the development, implementation, and management of the DMP Policies and Procedures, in compliance with all federal, state, and local regulations applicable to a 501c3 nonprofit organization and consistent with best management practices.

jobs.description:
Follow your passion

Are you looking to make a BIG impact? At Zeta, we pursue an unprecedented combination of high academic achievement and social-emotional development for our students. We insist that every student receives a world-class education while fostering a love for learning. We are passionate about changing the landscape of public education in New York City and beyond, and we are uncompromising in our mission.

Currently, we operate multiple elementary and middle schools in the Bronx, Upper Manhattan, and Queens.
We plan to grow and open 1-2 schools each year because children in every community deserve excellent, equitable education. Join our growing team today, and be a change agent for children.

Our Network office is located at 401 W. 218th St., New York, NY 10034. Our Network team follows a hybrid work schedule: in-person work is required Tuesdays and Thursdays. School-facing roles such as this one may also require physical presence on other days, as required. It is projected for this role that on a regular basis, 3 to 4 in-person days per week will be required on average. In the first 2-3 months, more in person days may be required for you to get up to speed.

Deliver powerful results

To achieve our vision, we are searching for a stellar Managing Director of Operations Transformation with a Bachelor's Degree and 10+ years of experience and a proven record of building, optimizing, and scaling operational systems. The position title will be commensurate with candidate experience.

Responsibilities:

In this role, you will focus on building and implementing the highest-priority, scalable operational systems across Zeta schools. Reporting to the Chief Operating Officer, Schools, and with input from the CEO, this role is pivotal in removing barriers to achieving consistent world-class operations as Zeta scales schools across New York City. Job Description Summary

The Director of Communications provides essential communication, digital media, and creative support for the Educating Character Initiative (ECI), a grant-funded project working to catalyze a movement in character education at colleges and universities across the U.S. Since 2023, the ECI has built a community of character among over 2600 individuals and 850 organizations / institutions; awarded nearly $60 million in grants to our partners; hosted educational and community-building webinars, conferences, convenings and other events; and become a major team in its unit, the Program for Leadership and Character at Wake Forest University, and a significant presence in character education around the world.

This position is responsible for developing and implementing a comprehensive communications strategy to successfully drive continued engagement with the ECI Community, encourage connection between members, amplify our grantees’ work, oversee storytelling about the impact of our work, contribute to the design and dissemination of character-related resources and reports, and attract participants to apply for grants. The role requires a style that encourages community-building, excellent written and verbal communication skills, the ability to communicate effectively with diverse audiences and stakeholders, and the interpersonal and organizational skills to collaborate with the Executive Director of the Educating Character Initiative and the Director of Collective Learning on a variety of projects. The Director of Communications may also support other communications activities of the Initiative and the Program for Leadership and Character on an as-needed basis. This is a grant-funded position supported by a multi-year grant from Lilly Endowment Inc.

Wake Forest University is a private, coeducational institution dedicated to academic excellence in liberal arts, graduate, and professional education. Located in Winston-Salem, NC (“The City of Arts and Innovation”), the University has a deep institutional commitment to public service and engagement with the world, as indicated by the motto Pro Humanitate (for humanity), which encourages students to develop the qualities of human character needed to serve humanity. With the aim to educate the whole person, the University has established an innovative Program for Leadership and Character that plans creative programming and courses to help students develop the character needed to lead inclusively in an increasingly complex world. The Program is based on cutting-edge academic research on leadership and character, including research conducted by Wake Forest faculty in various fields who are leading experts on the study of character. For more on the Program, see https://leadershipandcharacter.wfu.edu/.

Over the last few years, the Program for Leadership and Character has received major grants and gifts to develop leaders of character at Wake Forest and support other colleges and universities who seek to promote leadership and character on their campuses. We are now supporting a significant expansion of work to external partner institutions through the Educating Character Initiative, aimed at empowering and equipping other colleges and universities to educate character in their contexts. These efforts include support for major conferences and convenings on character; managing a community platform; developing character-related resources that faculty and staff can use to design and deliver courses and programming; and community-building and capacity-building grants to facilitate this work at other institutions. Details about the Educating Character Initiative are available here https://leadershipandcharacter.wfu.edu/eci/.

Please submit (1) a cover letter explaining your communications experience and your fit with the Educating Character Initiative; (2) a résumé or curriculum vitae; (3) a portfolio of 3-5 pieces of relevant communications work (stories, articles, newsletters, videos, posters, reports, etc.); and (4) three professional references (at least one of whom must be a current or former supervisor).

Deadline for priority consideration is October 18, 2026. This position is eligible for remote work. The position will remain open until filled.

This position is not eligible for sponsorship of non-immigrant or immigrant visa status through Wake Forest University. All eligible applicants are encouraged to apply.

Job Description

Essential Functions:

Develops and implements a strategic vision for communication to drive continued engagement with the ECI Community, encourage connection between members, and communicate the ECI’s reach, impact, and opportunities to a variety of audiences and stakeholders.
Sustains brand voice aligned with the Initiative’s values of hospitality, humility, and common purpose to build an engaged, connected community from a variety of academic and professional backgrounds.
Manages storytelling efforts about faculty, staff, students, and events that convey the value of character and character programming, the impact and reach of the ECI, the connections forming within the ECI Community, and the importance of research, scholarship, and creative activity related to character in higher education.
Directs content creation (e.g. social media posts, emails, videos, reports, etc.) to share the work of the Educating Character Initiative (ECI) in ways that align with the mission, content, and style of Wake Forest and the Program for Leadership and Character (PLC).
Collaborates with an external vendor and the Senior Director of Communications for the Program for Leadership and Character to create homepage content for a new networking platform for character educators.
Serves as creative director for a community platform, enabling institutions to showcase their work and attract collaborators and funders.
Oversees internal and external communication efforts — including web text, newsletters, social posts, event participant email updates, grant acceptance/rejection notifications, articles, and more — related to Educating Character Initiative grants, events, partnerships, and requests for proposals.
Writes, designs, and delivers newsletters, articles, and social media profiles and communications that share compelling stories of impact and opportunity.
Manages and updates ECI websites and web platforms, including keeping event registration portals up to date.
Communicates to internal and external audiences about all grant activities, including Requests for Proposals (RFPs), awards, information sessions, impact, and scholarship.
Assists with ECI and PLC conferences and event planning, execution, evaluation, and communication.
Develops, sustains, and expands a strong digital media presence to advertise events, communicate impact, and highlight achievements.
Assists with writing annual reports to the University and funding agencies.
Collaborates with the University Marketing and Communications office, including Design, Writing, Video, Digital, News & Media Relations, and Events, on news and announcements that may require coordinated messaging, appeal to a wider University audience, and/ or draw external media interest.
Collaborates with ECI staff to host online activities and events, including Advisory Board meetings, monthly online workshops, and summer programming.
Coordinates with outside consultants, contractors, and partners for writing, graphic design, video production, and communications strategy as needed, and manages communications budget.
Supports other Communications activities for the Program on an as-needed basis.
Position may grow to include supervision of other members of the ECI team.
Performs other duties as assigned.

Required Education, Knowledge, Skills, Abilities

Bachelor’s degree with five or more years of related experience.
Exceptional ability to communicate effectively, both verbally and in writing; strong command of grammar, diction, and English usage in professional communications, including accuracy in proofreading, composing correspondence, editing, and typing.
The ability to think creatively, communicate strategically, and expand a range of relevant audiences.
Demonstrated ability to be a self-starter with a strong work ethic who takes initiative, works with minimal supervision, and completes tasks without prompting.
Capacity to lead the messaging for a complex, evolving, mission-driven initiative. This includes understanding the mission, tracking core conceptual language, tailoring messaging for discrete context, and being out ahead in framing what is next.
Excellent organizational and time-management skills; ability to manage multiple tasks simultaneously.
Excellent interpersonal skills and the ability to work professionally, courteously, and effectively with a wide range of constituencies in a diverse community, including faculty, staff, and administrators.
High degree of professionalism, integrity, and dependability.
Commitment to supporting the intellectual and ethical development of students, faculty, and staff and the capacity of partner institutions.
Demonstrated ability to maintain strict confidentiality of sensitive information and records in accordance with state and federal laws and professional ethics; ability to manage and distribute information appropriately.
Ability to represent the Educating Character Initiative, the Program for Leadership and Character, and Wake Forest University in a professional manner and in alignment with the mission and vision of the Program and University.
Openness to feedback and a commitment to personal and professional growth.
Proficiency with technology and computers, including demonstrated ability to use Microsoft Office (Word, Excel, and PowerPoint) and the ability to learn website management and other relevant software.
Ability to positively support and supervise direct reports.

Preferred Education, Knowledge, Skills, Abilities

Experience in higher education.
Experience in community engagement or organizing.
Experience with graphic design.
Experience with digital storytelling.
Experience with large and small-scale on-site and remote conferences and programming.

Accountabilities

Reports to the Director of Collective Learning for the Education Character Initiative, Program for Leadership and Character. Receives feedback and support from the Senior Director of Communications, Program for Leadership and Character.
Supports ECI grants, education, operations, scholars, and research teams with communication needs.
Responsible for own work.
Communicating with internal and external stakeholders in a manner that reflects the mission and vision of the Educating Character Initiative, the Program for Leadership and Character, and Wake Forest University.

No adverse environmental conditions expected.

Job Title:
Chief Advancement Officer

Job Type: Full Time

Job Summary

The California Academy of Sciences seeks a Chief Advancement Officer to lead a division at an inflection point. The Academy is a scientifically rigorous, globally respected institution moving through a period of real change, including two rounds of layoffs, a newly ratified collective bargaining agreement, and a period of heightened external scrutiny. Despite these challenges, the internal culture and momentum are improving and reflect enthusiasm for the future. This is a hands-on role for a builder who can stabilize and re-energize a large, talented division and forge real partnerships with scientists, educators, and Board members who are eager to be activated as partners in philanthropy.

Looking ahead, the Academy is building towards a comprehensive campaign spanning capital, operating, and endowment priorities. The incoming Chief of Advancement will help shape this campaign’s scope and sequencing from the ground up, in close partnership with the Executive Director and Board.

Full Job Description

THIS POSITION IS HYBRID. THE SUCCESSFUL CANDIDATE WILL BE IN THE SAN FRANCISCO OFFICE FOUR DAYS A WEEK.

About The California Academy Of Sciences

Founded in 1853, the California Academy of Sciences (the Academy) is a globally renowned, AZA-accredited non-profit scientific and cultural institution located in the heart of San Francisco’s Golden Gate Park. Home to a world-class planetarium, aquarium, rainforest, research institute, and natural history museum—all under one living roof—the Academy’s mission is to regenerate the natural world through science, learning, and collaboration.

The Academy’s living collection reflects Earth’s vast biodiversity, consisting of nearly 60,000 animals representing over 800 species. Its research collections are the largest west of the Mississippi, spanning nearly 46 million plants, animals, fossils, and cultural artifacts from across the globe and throughout history. Its diverse team includes leading biodiversity scientists, educators, storytellers, designers, and communicators who are passionate about advancing knowledge and catalyzing action through science and storytelling.

Organizational Culture

The California Academy of Sciences invites new staff members to join as part of a mission-driven community that values curiosity, collaboration, and innovation, and celebrates its accomplishments together. Staff share a commitment to executing a new strategic plan that will strengthen the organization’s financial foundations, cultivate a vibrant internal culture, and foster smart growth to secure the Academy’s future.

The Academy is looking for candidates who excel in their field and take pride in their work. Candidates may come from a number of different backgrounds and experiences and are encouraged to apply whether or not you believe you meet every competency for the position.

OPPORTUNITY HIGHLIGHTS

Salary Range: $325,000 – $350,000

Benefits Include

5 weeks of vacation, in addition to holidays, sick time, and floating holidays

Medical, Vision, Dental Insurance

403b

YOU ARE

An enthusiastic, activating doer with strong personal follow-through

An enterprise thinker who partners naturally across science, education, communications, and governance

A leader who embodies a growth mindset, with proven experience demonstrating success

A talented, respected, and gifted storyteller

A thoughtful and generous leader who supports and promotes their team

Deeply rooted in Bay Area philanthropy

Position Overview

The California Academy of Sciences seeks a Chief Advancement Officer to lead a division at an inflection point. The Academy is a scientifically rigorous, globally respected institution moving through a period of real change, including two rounds of layoffs, a newly ratified collective bargaining agreement, and a period of heightened external scrutiny. Despite these challenges, the internal culture and momentum are improving and reflect enthusiasm for the future. This is a hands-on role for a builder who can stabilize and re-energize a large, talented division and forge real partnerships with scientists, educators, and Board members who are eager to be activated as partners in philanthropy.

Looking ahead, the Academy is building towards a comprehensive campaign spanning capital, operating, and endowment priorities. The incoming Chief of Advancement will help shape this campaign’s scope and sequencing from the ground up, in close partnership with the Executive Director and Board.

The Academy is concurrently conducting a search for its next Executive Director. The Chief of Advancement hire is expected to serve as a compatible, strong, activating fundraising partner to the incoming Executive Director, especially in the early days of that transition.

REPORTING RELATIONSHIP

The Chief Advancement Officer reports to the Executive Director and serves as a member of the Senior Leadership Team. The role oversees a division of approximately 18-20 staff organized across leadership giving, corporate & foundation partnerships, donor events, planned giving, and development operations.

Primary Responsibilities

Fundraising Strategy & Revenue Growth

Build and lead a culture of philanthropy across the Advancement division and the institution as a whole

Ensure direct, trusted working relationships with scientists, educators, and Board members and activate them as partners in fundraising

Identify fundraising needs across existing programs and build attainable near- and long-term strategies spanning annual giving, capital campaigns, planned giving, special events, and endowment

Explore new revenue streams by evaluating and refining donor solicitation, cultivation, communication, and recognition/affinity programs, as a way to keep donors informed and connected to the Academy’s mission, work, and accomplishments

Regularly evaluate and adjust fundraising strategies, leveraging internal relationships and Board members to increase revenue and participation, and recommend cultivation and solicitation visits to major donors and prospects

Take a hands-on, active role with major and strategic donors and maintain ongoing communication with executive leadership and the Board to ensure buy-in to fundraising initiatives at the highest level

Portfolio Management & Board Relations

Support Board members in every aspect of their philanthropic journey, including their personal commitment to the Academy and their relationships with various public and private funders and philanthropists

Staff and prepare the Board in a strategy for increased participation and eventual campaigns

Lead a traditional advancement portfolio, including annual fund, membership, major and principal gifts, and planned giving

Maintain a personal portfolio of the organization’s most sophisticated and generous donors

Position the division for a comprehensive campaign

Diversification of Funding Sources

Evaluate and grow corporate and foundation partnerships alongside individual giving, including sponsorship and IP-partnership opportunities

Support pursuit of government, agency, and institutional grant funding in partnership with science and program leadership

Expand planned giving and endowment strategies to diversify the Academy’s long-term funding base

Development Operations, Technology, & Data

Oversee development operations, including the donor database/CRM, gift processing, and prospect research infrastructure

Use data and reporting to inform fundraising strategy, track progress against goals, and support Board- and Senior Leadership Team-level decision-making

Evaluate current systems and processes for opportunities to improve efficiency and staff productivity

Team Leadership & Internal Management

Recruit, coach, nurture, and retain a high-performing team; provide an environment that encourages stability as well as a growth mindset, while holding the team accountable to ambitious goals

Provide leadership that challenges, inspires, and motivates people across the Academy’s local, national, and global community

Demonstrate a proven ability to recruit, mentor, lead, and develop a diverse staff, with a track record of building high-performing, loyal teams

Lead with a flexible, inclusive style that adapts to different audiences and sharpens colleagues’ focus

Serve as a positive, unifying figure who leads by influence and example to build an integrated development culture across the Academy

Demonstrate a commitment to transparency that builds trust and confidence in the advancement operation across the institution

Manage the division’s budget, staffing, and day-to-day operations

Serve as a steady, credible, and enthusiastic voice on the Senior Leadership Team during a period of institutional change

Foster a culture of respect, communication, and accountability within the team

Champion the Academy’s culture of equity, diversity, and inclusion, bringing commitment, ideas, and energy to diversity efforts across the workforce, donor base, and broader community

COMPETENCIES

Ideal Candidate Statement

The ideal candidate is a seasoned information technology executive with at least five years of progressively responsible experience leading an information technology department, and a current Certified Information Systems Security Professional (CISSP) or Certified Information Security Manager (CISM) demonstrating deep expertise in cybersecurity, infrastructure, and regulatory compliance. They combine strategic, big-picture thinking with hands-on operational skill, equally comfortable setting districtwide technology vision, managing budgets and vendor contracts, and directing the day-to-day security, network, and systems work that keeps a college running. This person mentors and develops technical staff, builds trust across administrators, staff, faculty and governance committees, and communicates complex technical issues clearly to non-technical stakeholders. Above all, they bring a genuine, equity-minded commitment to serving a culturally diverse community college population, along with the adaptability and independent judgment needed to navigate evolving technology, risk, and public policy landscapes.

Position Description

Under the direction of the Vice President, Administrative Services, the Executive Director of Information Technology Services provides districtwide leadership and technology planning. The incumbent manages a highly skilled workforce including technical and management level staff in a culturally diverse environment and works collaboratively to support faculty innovation in academic learning environments. The Executive Director of Information Technology Services plans, organizes, controls, and directs the technology operations for the college. The incumbent provides technical recommendations regarding hardware and software for the district for both instructional and administrative use. In addition, the incumbent provides executive oversight for the college's information security program, leads the strategic design, implementation and enforcement of policies to protect critical data, mitigate cyber risk and ensure compliance with regulatory standards.

Duties And Responsibilities

Technology Operations Management: Provides strategic technical guidance to the Vice President of Administrative Services, assessing institutional IT needs and recommending solutions. Oversees and improves information services, including distance education support, telecommunications, networking, classroom technology, and user support. Administers a district-wide IT infrastructure and integrated systems (e.g., Colleague and third-party products), ensuring service alignment with instructional and administrative needs. Stays current on technology trends, systems design, cybersecurity, and relevant public policy in higher education. Directs IT operations, including network security, systems analysis, maintenance, and staff training. Ensures compliance with federal, state, and institutional regulations, and manages documentation and reporting. Leads long-term IT planning and policy development in collaboration with stakeholders, focusing on continuous process improvement. Implements and manages infrastructure and application projects using project management best practices. Oversees key systems such as website, email, backups, virtual environments, and networks (wired, wireless, and telecommunications). Ensures accessibility compliance across all district-wide IT systems.
Oversight of Information Security: Evaluates the college's information security needs and implements information security measures to protect the information and technology resources of the district; Works with third party vendors as needed and with district departments to mitigate risks and threats to information security. Develops procedures for an annual information security audit and leads the review in coordination with other essential departments. Advises executive leadership of results and risks. Coordinates with Risk Management and Campus Police Services and other law enforcement agencies to report and resolve information security incidents.
Information Technology Staff Management: Provide guidance, leadership, and mentoring to a team of professionals. Plan for and manage recruitment, orientation, and continued training and education of staff to support and develop the technical expertise needed to meet long-term business needs. Manage staff by reviewing, approving and allocating work and work assignments. Supervise and evaluate the performance of assigned staff and recommend transfers, reassignment, termination and disciplinary actions as needed.
Budget Management: Analyzes staffing, equipment, and supply needs and manages the department budget. Monitors actual-to-budget expenditures, adjusting expenditure patterns/trends as needed to comply with budgeted amounts. Authorizes and tracks expenditures to forecast future needs and provides supportive documentation for proposed expenses. Assists the Vice President of Administrative Services in the development and preparation of the annual budget forecast for the Information Technology Services department. Prepares cost estimates and specifications for purchase and maintenance of college technology assets and develop RFQs and RFPs for information system and technology related services. Evaluate materials, products and services. Recommend and implement technology related acquisitions. Engages in the district's program review process to assess workload and staffing, administrative support systems, internal reporting relationships, and technology needs. Identifies and implements approved program improvement objectives to further enhance the efficiency and effectiveness of service delivery methods and procedures.
Community Engagement and Vendor Management: Represents the district and participates in meetings, workshops, and governance committees to identify issues, develop solutions, and support collaboration across campus groups. Engages with faculty, staff, administrators, and students to support participatory governance and process improvement initiatives. Coordinates with user and technical teams to assess system needs and develop application solutions. Manages vendor relationships, including contract negotiations, licensing, and service agreements, and acts as the main liaison with external partners and regulatory bodies. Promotes equity, diversity, and inclusion by implementing culturally responsive, service-oriented strategies and supporting historically minoritized groups.

District Statement

Founded in 1967, Ohlone College is named in honor of the early Ohlone People who inhabited the San Francisco Bay Area. Ohlone College is committed to providing a high-quality education to serve our diverse population of over 15,000 students per year. Ohlone College is nationally recognized for our Deaf Studies and Interpreter Preparation programs, and is widely known for our nursing, health sciences, liberal arts, biomedical science, and smart manufacturing programs. As a learning community, we embrace and champion inclusivity, integrity, student expression, global citizenship, and continuous improvement.

Blue Star Families

Blue Star Families is the largest nonprofit dedicated to making military life better for families. Each year, we support over 1.5 million military- and veteran-connected family members through a national network of 300,000+ members and local chapters in communities across the country.

Our mission is simple and bold: We make military life awesome for families.

We listen, share, partner, and act to deliver evidence-based, data-driven solutions that work for real people. We’re a lifestyle organization, a friend and neighbor, and a trusted partner. Our approach is collaborative, human-centered, and designed with the whole family in mind.

A Blue Star Family is one with an immediate family member — a spouse, parent, or child — actively serving in the U.S. Armed Forces, including the Guard and Reserves. These families face unique challenges: frequent relocations, deployments, career disruption, and isolation. We respond with research-informed programs that create connection, build resilience, and foster a true sense of belonging.

We serve with urgency but build trust over time — because change happens at the speed of trust. Whether we’re driving spouse employment, supporting caregivers, or helping communities welcome military families, we strive for upstream solutions.

Solve complex challenges with data, heart, and humility

General Description

The Director, Development for the National Capital Region “Flagship” Chapter is responsible for assisting in local fundraising efforts, cultivating donor relationships, and supporting the development of strategic partnerships to support the chapter’s financial sustainability and growth. This role partners closely with the Chapter Executive Director and the national Development team to align local fundraising strategies with Blue Star Families’ mission and organizational goals.

The Director will steward a portfolio of individual, corporate, and foundation donors and support grant writing and reporting in collaboration with the national team.

While this role is remote, periodic out-of-town, overnight travel is an essential function. Team members are expected to travel several times per year for offsites, planning sessions, and company-wide gatherings. These events are essential for contributing to team outcomes, building trust across the organization, and staying aligned in a distributed environment. Participation in these in-person gatherings is a required part of the role and integral to successful performance in our remote-first organization.

The Director must reside in the local community the Chapter serves. Preference will be given to candidates who have resided in the designated Chapter community for a minimum of the past three years.

Collaborate with the Executive Director and national Development team to identify and pursue funding opportunities aligned with chapter programs and goals.
Collaborate with the Executive Director on donor recognition and ensure consistent, high-quality communication with funders and supporters.
Support the development and execution of donor engagement events and activities.

Perform other duties as assigned.

7+ years of relevant experience in fundraising for a nonprofit organization
Demonstrated success in individual giving, corporate sponsorships, grant writing, and/or planning and executing major fundraising events.
Strong relationship-building and communication skills.
Self-starter with the ability to work both independently and collaboratively.
Experience with CRM software (e.g., Salesforce).
Local travel requirements required outside of your home office will be up to 40% or less depending on business needs.
Ability to travel out of town overnight several times per year for staff offsites, planning retreats, and company-wide events. These gatherings are essential for connection, brainstorming, and staying strategically aligned across teams. Participation is required as a core part of the role.

Desired Experience, Skills & Background

Bachelor’s degree preferred

Familiarity with membership-driven organizations

Knowledge of the local philanthropic landscape and funding community

More About Blue Star Families

Blue Star Families empowers military and Veteran families to thrive by connecting them with their civilian neighbors — both people and organizations — to create strong communities of mutual support. We believe we're all stronger when we take care of one another.

Our groundbreaking research is raising the nation's awareness of the unique challenges of military family life. With the help of neighbors across the country, Blue Star Families is overcoming the isolation and alienation of frequent moves, deployments, and reduced support from the government. Our innovative programs are solving specific challenges for military families, including fighting economic insecurity with resources that foster spouse career development, creating family strength with rich family programming, and providing critical peer support for caregivers, whose numbers are only increasing.

Job Description Summary

The Director of Communications provides essential communication, digital media, and creative support for the Educating Character Initiative (ECI), a grant-funded project working to catalyze a movement in character education at colleges and universities across the U.S. Since 2023, the ECI has built a community of character among over 2600 individuals and 850 organizations / institutions; awarded nearly $60 million in grants to our partners; hosted educational and community-building webinars, conferences, convenings and other events; and become a major team in its unit, the Program for Leadership and Character at Wake Forest University, and a significant presence in character education around the world.

This position is responsible for developing and implementing a comprehensive communications strategy to successfully drive continued engagement with the ECI Community, encourage connection between members, amplify our grantees’ work, oversee storytelling about the impact of our work, contribute to the design and dissemination of character-related resources and reports, and attract participants to apply for grants. The role requires a style that encourages community-building, excellent written and verbal communication skills, the ability to communicate effectively with diverse audiences and stakeholders, and the interpersonal and organizational skills to collaborate with the Executive Director of the Educating Character Initiative and the Director of Collective Learning on a variety of projects. The Director of Communications may also support other communications activities of the Initiative and the Program for Leadership and Character on an as-needed basis. This is a grant-funded position supported by a multi-year grant from Lilly Endowment Inc.

Wake Forest University is a private, coeducational institution dedicated to academic excellence in liberal arts, graduate, and professional education. Located in Winston-Salem, NC (“The City of Arts and Innovation”), the University has a deep institutional commitment to public service and engagement with the world, as indicated by the motto Pro Humanitate (for humanity), which encourages students to develop the qualities of human character needed to serve humanity. With the aim to educate the whole person, the University has established an innovative Program for Leadership and Character that plans creative programming and courses to help students develop the character needed to lead inclusively in an increasingly complex world. The Program is based on cutting-edge academic research on leadership and character, including research conducted by Wake Forest faculty in various fields who are leading experts on the study of character. For more on the Program, see https://leadershipandcharacter.wfu.edu/.

Over the last few years, the Program for Leadership and Character has received major grants and gifts to develop leaders of character at Wake Forest and support other colleges and universities who seek to promote leadership and character on their campuses. We are now supporting a significant expansion of work to external partner institutions through the Educating Character Initiative, aimed at empowering and equipping other colleges and universities to educate character in their contexts. These efforts include support for major conferences and convenings on character; managing a community platform; developing character-related resources that faculty and staff can use to design and deliver courses and programming; and community-building and capacity-building grants to facilitate this work at other institutions. Details about the Educating Character Initiative are available here https://leadershipandcharacter.wfu.edu/eci/.

Please submit (1) a cover letter explaining your communications experience and your fit with the Educating Character Initiative; (2) a résumé or curriculum vitae; (3) a portfolio of 3-5 pieces of relevant communications work (stories, articles, newsletters, videos, posters, reports, etc.); and (4) three professional references (at least one of whom must be a current or former supervisor).

Deadline for priority consideration is October 18, 2026. This position is eligible for remote work. The position will remain open until filled.

This position is not eligible for sponsorship of non-immigrant or immigrant visa status through Wake Forest University. All eligible applicants are encouraged to apply.

Job Description

Essential Functions:

Develops and implements a strategic vision for communication to drive continued engagement with the ECI Community, encourage connection between members, and communicate the ECI’s reach, impact, and opportunities to a variety of audiences and stakeholders.
Sustains brand voice aligned with the Initiative’s values of hospitality, humility, and common purpose to build an engaged, connected community from a variety of academic and professional backgrounds.
Manages storytelling efforts about faculty, staff, students, and events that convey the value of character and character programming, the impact and reach of the ECI, the connections forming within the ECI Community, and the importance of research, scholarship, and creative activity related to character in higher education.
Directs content creation (e.g. social media posts, emails, videos, reports, etc.) to share the work of the Educating Character Initiative (ECI) in ways that align with the mission, content, and style of Wake Forest and the Program for Leadership and Character (PLC).
Collaborates with an external vendor and the Senior Director of Communications for the Program for Leadership and Character to create homepage content for a new networking platform for character educators.
